name: Membrane Transport, Lipid Rafts and Channelopathies

reference.source: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry / Medical Biochemistry 5th ed
clinicalPearls: Membrane phospholipid asymmetry is maintained by ATP-dependent flippases and floppases; exteriorization of phosphatidylserine signals apoptosis
Lipid rafts are ordered cholesterol- and sphingolipid-rich microdomains that cluster signaling receptors and GPI-anchored proteins
Sodium-potassium ATPase exports 3 Na+ and imports 2 K+ per ATP hydrolyzed, generating transmembrane resting potential
Cystic fibrosis results from CFTR gene mutations (most commonly F508del), an ATP-gated chloride channel
CFTR dysfunction prevents chloride and water secretion into airways, causing thick dehydrated mucus and chronic infections
reference.pathophysiology: Lipid bilayers provide semipermeable barriers separating intra- and extracellular ionic environments. Integral membrane transport proteins regulate solute flux via facilitated diffusion, primary ATP-driven pumps, or secondary coupled cotransport. Channelopathies arise from mutations in ion channel pores, disrupting electrochemical homeostasis, cellular volume regulation, and epithelial fluid secretion.
additionalDifferentials: Cystic fibrosis vs primary ciliary dyskinesia (Kartagener syndrome)
Congenital long QT syndromes (KCNQ1 / KCNH2 potassium channel mutations)
Bartter and Gitelman syndromes (renal tubular channelopathies)
additionalInvestigations: Sweat chloride quantitative pilocarpine iontophoresis (positive if >=60 mmol/L for cystic fibrosis)
CFTR genetic mutation panel and full gene sequencing
Serum electrolytes and arterial blood gas for metabolic alkalosis
High-resolution chest CT for bronchiectasis and mucus plugging
